decision_tree.text:
# C2 decision tree: what does a nominated pair of quantities actually compare?

Written before recoding any record or issuing any second reading in this pass.

## The object

A historical pair names two reported quantities (outputs) in one paper. The earlier
synthesis treated such a pair as a "mixed" result: favourable on one quantity,
unfavourable on the other. The tree asks what the located source passages allow one
to compare. It assigns exactly one category.

Terms. A *run pair* is a baseline calculation B and an alternative calculation A of
the same flow case and conditions that differ by a named change of wall treatment or
near-wall boundary implementation (anything else that also changes is recorded).
A *reference* is the measurement or higher-fidelity calculation both runs are compared
with for that output. The *direction* for an output is whether A is closer to or
farther from the reference than B in absolute discrepancy.

## Questions, in order

Q1. Run identity. In the located passages, is each of the two outputs reported for
    the same run pair (the same B and the same A)?
    - The two outputs come from different flow cases, operating points, Reynolds
      numbers or sets of runs, with no run pair common to both -> `different_tests`.
    - Each output has its own contrast between runs, but the two contrasts do not use
      the same B and A -> `no_shared_baseline`.
    - Both outputs are reported for the same run or runs, but for at least one output
      there is only one wall treatment, so nothing can be ranked (Q5: no treatment
      baseline) -> `shared_runs_no_treatment_baseline`.
    - Yes -> Q2.

Q2. Reference. Is there, for each output, one reference against which both B and A
    are compared? If an output has none -> `matched_no_common_reference`.
    Otherwise -> Q3.

Q3. Support. For each output note the support on which the direction is assessed:
    "complete" (every station, height, tap or time the source reports for that output
    on these runs, or the source's own global or integrated measure) or "restricted"
    (one station, a height range, a subset of taps or an instant chosen within a larger
    reported support).

Q4. Direction of each output: closer / farther / unresolved. For tabulated numbers
    apply the frozen C1 rule (rounding box and reported reference interval). For
    curves use the source's own statement of direction or a separation clearly larger
    than the line or marker width; otherwise unresolved. A discrepancy that B and A
    share (both miss the reference by about the same amount) is "unresolved", not
    "farther".

Leaves after Q4:
    - Both directions resolved and opposite, both on complete support (or both at the
      same single station and time, where that station is all the source reports)
      -> `matched_opposing_same_support`.
    - Opposite directions that exist only with at least one output on restricted
      support, or with the two outputs at different stations of a larger reported
      support -> `opposing_point_estimates_on_restricted_support`.
    - Not opposing on complete support, but the direction for an output changes sign
      when its support is restricted -> `matched_support_dependent`.
    - Otherwise -> `matched_no_opposing_rank`, with `matched_detail` one of
      `concordant` (both resolved, same sign), `one_direction_unresolved`,
      `both_unresolved_or_common_miss`.

## Closed vocabulary

`different_tests`, `no_shared_baseline`, `shared_runs_no_treatment_baseline`,
`matched_no_common_reference`, `matched_no_opposing_rank` (+ `matched_detail`),
`matched_support_dependent`, `opposing_point_estimates_on_restricted_support`,
`matched_opposing_same_support`.

Earlier labels map as follows: `matched_subset_no_opposing_rank` ->
`matched_no_opposing_rank` with `subset_only: true`; `different_criteria_no_adverse_delta`
-> decided again by the tree (the earlier label is kept in `legacy_adjudication`).

## Reading procedure

First reading: the existing records (written before this tree) are recoded from their
own fields; the source is opened wherever a field does not decide a branch.
Second reading: a reader who is given the pair's two quantities and original locators,
this tree and the source file, and none of the first reading's category, inference or
direction. Second readings cover every pair whose first-reading category is not
`different_tests`, a seeded random ten of the `different_tests` pairs
(numpy default_rng(20261119), drawn without replacement from the sorted pair IDs), and
the same-run contrasts that the paper or response uses outside the 79
(N655 at t* = 0.2, N626 four to five message-passing steps, N174).

Agreement is reported on the category (and on the grouped question "is there a run
pair with both outputs: yes/no"). Both readings are kept. A disagreement is settled
by citing the source passage, and the settled category is recorded with its reason.

## What the categories can and cannot support

The 79 pairs were nominated because the earlier coding called them mixed. The
categories describe what those nominations compared. They do not estimate how often
rankings reverse between quantities in the literature.

## Amendment 1 (made before any record was recoded and before any second reading was issued)

Some nominated pairs compare two runs that differ by grid resolution, outer closure
or a whole package, with the wall law unchanged. Q1 therefore accepts any run pair B, A
that differs by a named change, and the reader records `intervention_type`:
`wall treatment`, `near-wall implementation or sampling`, `grid`, `outer closure`,
`whole system or several changes`. Categories are assigned as above. Tabulations that
concern the effect of a wall treatment use only the first two types.

fixed.note: The text stored here is the fixed file with internal file and role names removed. Nothing else differs.

amendment_2_after_second_readings: Where the source offers more than one run pair for the two outputs, each is recorded. The pair-level category is taken from a change of wall treatment or near-wall implementation at fixed grid and numerics where one exists.
A verbal statement that the unplotted runs are "almost identical" counts as a source-stated unresolved direction for those runs.

A restricted-support leaf requires the source's own statement of the local reversal or a recorded numerical reading with its half-width. A visual impression without a recorded half-width is flagged as a possible local reversal and does not move the leaf.
Where the source states that the direction of one output differs between its components (for example stress components), the leaf is matched_support_dependent.
